'As an additional cost to play Hungering Slaughterbeast, banish 3 random cards from your graveyard.' + printed **Blood Debt**. Shadow Brute Action - Attack (Monarch).

BLOOD DEBT NOT AUTHORED: printed_keywords carries BloodDebt - a CR section 8 keyword on the card DB keywords field, implemented engine-side (ability_keywords.blood_debt: lose 1{h} at end phase per face-up banished instance). Re-authoring it would be a defect.

COST PLACEMENT - CARD LEVEL, NOT A COST-ONLY PLAY ABILITY. This replaces an earlier draft in this directory that used ability-level additional_cost with "effects": []: test_card_json_hygiene.test_every_ability_has_effects fails ANY ability whose effects list is empty (its NO_EFFECTS_REQUIRED exempts only COST_MODIFIER/REPLACEMENT/DEFEND_RESTRICTION/FREEZE_WHILE/GRANT_ATTACK_WHILE - read this session, tests/test_card_json_hygiene.py:31-35), so that shape is a hygiene defect by construction even though DSL_REFERENCE's Scrap snippet shows it. The card's only authored behaviour IS the cost, so it goes in the top-level 'cost' object: the hygiene test counts a card-level cost as implementation (tests/test_card_json_hygiene.py:196-200), and the engine path is verified end to end this session - loader compiles the top-level cost dict into CardDef.play_cost (loader.py:148-151), play.py CHECKS play_cost.check_fn before offering the play (play.py:567-568) and PAYS pay_fn on application (play.py:1146-1147). It therefore still BLOCKS the play when unpayable, which is what a mandatory additional cost requires ('costs are costs, not effects'). Shape copied from .drafts/boneyard_marauder_blue/_yellow.json, whose printed first sentence is identical.

BANISH_RANDOM_FROM_GRAVEYARD (cost_types.py:192-224) reads exactly one parameter, amount (default 1): can_pay requires >= N cards in the controller's graveyard; pay random.sample()s N cards - 'random', not chosen - and banishes each via canonical banish(origin_zone='graveyard'), so they actually leave the graveyard (no double-zone bug). Mandatory and unchosen, matching the printed text. The attack itself needs no authored ability: an Action - Attack card is put onto the combat chain by the engine from its type/subtype when played.

No gaps.
